panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Three visibly separate cards rest on the operations table: COLD-STICKING HATCH, CONFLICTING HANDOFF CHECKLISTS and I MISS HOME ON LATE SHIFT. Pixa reads them without collapsing their purposes.
PANEL 2 — Mira examines the hatch report with a scanner at hand but leaves the personal card untouched; she can investigate the physical fault, not the feeling.
PANEL 3 — Astra reaches toward the anonymous personal card and asks about its author. Glorp turns it face-down to preserve the box's promise of anonymity.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb looks at the handwriting on the card while Noola, standing nearby, dryly rejects his amateur-detective impulse. Keep their exchange private and not an accusation.

PANEL 5 — Pixa leaves the personal author field blank while Astra sends the hatch fault to maintenance and Glorp takes the conflicting checklists for ordinary process repair. Three distinct outcomes remain visually separate.

summary: Five separate beats distinguish equipment reports, process confusion, and an anonymous personal disclosure. Pixa and Mira resist falsely interpreting the cards, Glorp defends anonymity, Kreeb exposes his temptation to recognize handwriting, and the crew routes only the actual repair work.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Kreeb places the anonymous personal card into the quiet room's local envelope. Noola enters, identifies the I MISS HOME ON LATE SHIFT card as hers, and stays by the open doorway.

PANEL 2 — Seated in a quiet two-shot, Noola explains missing home without wanting a repair ticket, and Kreeb recognizes how often he tries to fix her feelings or her water rig. The card remains private.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb offers company rather than a procedure. Noola permits him to sit but leaves her feelings unmeasured. End with quiet space around the pair, not a successful counseling-session pose.

summary: In the quiet room, Noola privately acknowledges writing the card about missing home on late shift. Kreeb initially treats that as something to fix but comes to understand she wanted a place to say it. No personal disclosure is added to the work board.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The afternoon operations work board records several completed mechanical fixes and one reconciled checklist, with no personal disclosure or inferred authors listed. Glorp points to the properly closed noise complaint.
PANEL 2 — Glorp replaces the conflicting handoff pages with one working checklist; Kreeb confirms that the operational information was sufficient to find the defect.
PANEL 3 — Noola passes the repaired corridor and acknowledges that someone else's shift will now be quieter. Astra agrees that the physical outcome matters more than identifying a person.
PANEL 4 — Pixa returns the repaired stool and files the equipment trace without names from the personal cards. In the background Kreeb lets Noola pass without asking for an emotional update.
PANEL 1 — Pixa points out the central dashboard's notice: LOW CATEGORY COMPLETION MAY LIMIT INTERPRETABILITY. The work board remains visibly full of actual closures.
PANEL 2 — Astra reads the demand for inferred disclosure categories and insists that completed repairs count without profiling coworkers.
PANEL 3 — Mira looks at the lab results: no demonstrated relationship between the physical residue measurements and personal cards. Kreeb seals the private envelope nearby.
PANEL 4 — Glorp keeps only the completed operational tasks in the outgoing data while Pixa retains empty inference fields; the request for categories remains visibly unanswered.
PANEL 5 — Kreeb reminds Astra that coworkers trusted the collection process not to turn their stories into scores. Astra holds the factual response ready to send.
